summary:
THE ORIGIN is an interactive browser-based workspace that helps students and researchers explore NASA microgravity combustion research. Built for the Flame in Freefall challenge, it brings together nine investigation summaries and 13 selected published test results from NASA sources.

Users can search findings, compare experimental conditions, inspect source references and explore study-specific charts. The platform preserves missing values and measurement warnings, helping users understand where comparisons are useful and where they could be misleading. Its evidence search uses local keyword matching to retrieve cited summaries, while transparent reading priorities help users decide what to investigate next.

THE ORIGIN makes complex combustion research easier to navigate and supports informed exploration of fire safety in space. It runs without installation or an API key and supports offline demonstrations and data exports. It is a research prototype, with independent scientific review still pending, rather than a validated fire-risk prediction system.
details:
THE ORIGIN is an interactive research workspace developed for the Flame in Freefall challenge. It helps students and researchers explore NASA microgravity combustion findings while understanding the experimental conditions behind them.

The application contains nine curated investigation summaries covering BASS, Saffire, FLEX, ACME and SAME, alongside a separate dataset of 13 selected published test rows from two NASA-hosted primary documents. Users can filter research by program, fuel and environment, compare investigation summaries, inspect original sources and export data as JSON or CSV.

Experimental Data provides separate BASS/BASS-II and Saffire visualizations. Each extracted row retains source references, units and relevant qualifications. Missing values remain missing, suspect oxygen measurements retain their warnings, and reused fuel remains labeled. Comparison checks highlight differences that could make conclusions misleading.

Evidence Search uses deterministic keyword matching to retrieve relevant, source-linked summaries. Research Priorities provides a transparent editorial reading order based on relevance, traceability and technical detail. Mission Applications distinguishes proposed uses from measured findings.

We built the frontend with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, using Node.js for bundling and automated tests. GitHub stores the source code, and GitHub Pages hosts the public application. The current features run entirely in the browser without a backend, account or API key. A self-contained HTML version supports offline demonstrations. The responsive interface includes decorative space animations, keyboard navigation and reduced-motion controls.

The creative contribution is a connected review workflow that makes provenance and comparison limits visible alongside the findings. Its intended impact is to make NASA combustion research easier to explore and support more informed research questions. We have not yet measured user impact.

All 13 automated software tests pass. The dataset is a deliberately selected published-data subset, and independent scientific review remains pending. Future work includes broader primary-source coverage, reconciliation with NASA PSI data and researcher usability evaluation.
